title: Anti-data center wave spreads to Europe and Asia, stalling roughly $42 billion in European investment
source_used: BigGo Finance relaying a CNBC report of 3 Oct 2026
key_facts: CNBC report of 3 Oct: negative sentiment toward data centers is growing in Europe and local opposition is rising in South Korea.
STL Partners data: opposition has affected about $42 billion of European data center investment; about $77 billion in the US.
European Data Center Monitor: more than 70 European projects rejected or restricted from January to April, more than in all of 2025.
Ireland suspended projects over power demand; Scotland paused planning approvals for new hyperscale data centers; Denmark passed emergency grid legislation; Spain requires 80% renewable power.
South Korea plans to require consent of a majority of residents within 200 metres of a site.
quote_evidence: Data from research firm STL Partners shows that public opposition has already affected approximately $42 billion in European data center investments, resulting in delays and cancellations.
According to a CNBC report on October 3, negative sentiment toward data centers is growing in Europe, where dense populations and high electricity prices prevail.
why_it_matters_hint: Data center opposition is no longer only an American story.
notes: Relay site; the CNBC original was not opened. The same page also gives a different US total (about $150 billion shelved or cancelled) from another source, a different measure than STL Partners' $77 billion.
